hook.situation: You are at a clinic or pharmacy and need to say symptoms clearly, explain what changed your day, and understand medicine instructions before you leave.
objectives: Describe symptoms with body part or symptom + 이/가 + 아프다/나다.
Explain causes with 아파서, 때문에, 니까, or 는 바람에 without mixing their tones.
Understand pharmacy directions like 식후에, 하루 세 번, and 드셔야 해요.
hook.whyItMatters: Health Korean is practical under pressure. A learner does not need random body words here; they need symptom phrases, clinic nouns, pharmacy nouns, and instruction patterns that can be used immediately.

grammarNotes.title: Symptom frame — body/symptom + 이/가
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Korean often makes the symptom or body part the subject: 목이 아파요, 열이 나요, 기침이 나요.
grammarNotes.formation: Body part + 이/가 아프다. Symptom noun + 이/가 나다/있다/심하다.

examples.en: My throat hurts.
examples.note: 목 is the subject of the pain.

examples.en: My stomach hurts, so I came to the clinic.
examples.note: 아파서 connects the symptom to the visit.

examples.en: I have a fever and I also have a cough.
examples.note: 열이 나다 and 기침이 나다 are natural symptom chunks.

examples.en: My headache was bad, so I could not sleep.

exceptions: Do not translate 'I have a fever' as 열을 가지고 있어요. Say 열이 나요.

grammarNotes.title: V아/어야 해요 — medical instruction or necessary action
grammarNotes.mentalModel: At a clinic, 아/어야 해요 turns advice into something the patient needs to do.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 아/어야 해요 to the verb stem. In respectful patient instructions, you may hear 드셔야 해요, 쉬셔야 해요, 오셔야 해요.

examples.en: You have to take the medicine after meals.
You have to rest at home today.

examples.ko: 열이 계속 나면 다시 와야 해요.
examples.romanization: yeori gyesok namyeon dasi waya haeyo.
examples.en: If the fever continues, you have to come back.
You have to drink a lot of water.

exceptions: 세요 is a direct polite instruction; 아/어야 해요 adds necessity. 쉬세요 = please rest. 쉬어야 해요 = you need to rest.

grammarNotes.title: A/V아서/어서 — symptom cause leading to result
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 아서/어서 is the calm cause-result link: I came because it hurts; I cannot sleep because I cough.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 아서/어서 to an adjective or verb stem. Use it for explanation, not for commands.

examples.en: My stomach hurts, so I came to the clinic.

examples.ko: 목이 아파서 말을 오래 못 해요.
examples.romanization: mogi apaseo mareul orae mot haeyo.
examples.en: My throat hurts, so I cannot talk for long.
I had a fever, so I rested for a day.
The cough was bad, so I could not sleep.

exceptions: For a request or instruction after the reason, 니까 usually sounds clearer: 열이 나니까 물을 많이 드세요.

grammarNotes.title: N 때문에 — because of a symptom or illness
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 때문에 names the problem as the cause. It often sounds like the symptom blocked or disrupted something.
grammarNotes.formation: N + 때문에. No subject/object particle goes between the noun and 때문에.

examples.en: I came to the clinic because of a cold.
I could not sleep because of the cough.
I could not work because of a headache.
My stomach feels uncomfortable because of the medicine.

exceptions: Say 감기 때문에, not 감기가 때문에. 때문에 attaches directly to the noun.

grammarNotes.title: A/V(으)니까 — since this is true, do this
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 니까 is useful when the symptom becomes a reason for advice, a request, or the next action.
grammarNotes.formation: Use 니까 after vowel stems and 으니까 after consonant stems. Descriptive verbs also use this pattern: 아프니까, 심하니까.

examples.ko: 열이 계속 나니까 물을 많이 드세요.
examples.romanization: yeori gyesok nanikka mureul mani deuseyo.
examples.en: Since the fever is continuing, drink a lot of water.

examples.ko: 목이 아프니까 말을 많이 하지 마세요.
examples.romanization: mogi apeunikka mareul mani haji maseyo.
examples.en: Since your throat hurts, do not talk a lot.
Since the cough is severe, come back.
Since you took the medicine, wait a little and see.

exceptions: For a plain past result, 아서/어서 often sounds more natural: 아파서 못 갔어요. 니까 is stronger when it leads to advice or a next step.

grammarNotes.title: V-는 바람에 — unexpected health problem disrupted something
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 는 바람에 says the event was unwanted and messed up the plan. In health contexts, it works with sudden symptoms or missed medicine.
grammarNotes.formation: Verb stem + 는 바람에 + usually negative/unwanted result in past tense.

examples.ko: 갑자기 열이 나는 바람에 수업에 못 갔어요.
examples.romanization: gapjagi yeori naneun barame sueobe mot gasseoyo.
examples.en: A fever suddenly came on, so I could not go to class.

examples.ko: 기침이 심해지는 바람에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.romanization: gichimi simhaejineun barame jameul mot jasseoyo.
examples.en: The cough got worse, so I could not sleep.
examples.note: The change caused an unwanted result.

examples.ko: 약을 깜빡하는 바람에 두통이 다시 심해졌어요.
examples.romanization: yageul kkamppakaneun barame dutongi dasi simhaejyeosseoyo.
examples.en: I forgot the medicine, so the headache got bad again.
examples.note: A mistake led to a bad result.

examples.ko: 배가 갑자기 아파지는 바람에 약속을 취소했어요.
examples.romanization: baega gapjagi apajineun barame yaksogeul chwisohesseoyo.
examples.en: My stomach suddenly started hurting, so I canceled the appointment.
examples.note: 바람에 carries the feeling that the plan was ruined.

exceptions: Do not use 는 바람에 for good results. For positive cause, use 덕분에. For neutral health explanation, use 아서/어서 or 때문에.

grammarNotes.title: V-는 중이에요 — current clinic or recovery action
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 는 중이에요 zooms in on what is happening right now: waiting, taking medicine, resting, or receiving treatment.
grammarNotes.formation: Verb stem + 는 중이에요. For noun situations, use N 중이에요: 진료 중이에요, 회복 중이에요.

examples.en: I am waiting for my appointment right now.
I am in the middle of taking medicine.
I am resting at home.
examples.note: Useful when updating someone after a clinic visit.

examples.en: I am still recovering.
examples.note: N 중이에요 works with recovery/status nouns.

exceptions: Do not use 는 중이에요 with static states like 아프다 as 아픈 중이에요 for this context. Say 아직 아파요 or 회복 중이에요.

exampleSentence.en: My stomach hurts, so I came to the clinic.
exampleSentence.note: In Korean, 병원 often covers neighborhood clinics too.

exampleSentence.en: I take the prescription to the pharmacy.

exampleSentence.note: In symptom talk, 목 often means throat.
Most natural first sentence for stomach pain.

exampleSentence.en: I have had a fever since this morning.
exampleSentence.note: Use 열이 나다 for having a fever.

exampleSentence.en: I could not sleep because of the cough.
I came to the clinic because of a cold.
exampleSentence.note: Common named cause in clinic talk.

exampleSentence.en: You have to take the medicine after meals.
I got a prescription at the clinic.
Take it three times a day after meals.
Take it three times a day.
I told the doctor my symptoms.
exampleSentence.note: 의사 선생님 is common in real clinic speech.

exampleSentence.en: I asked the pharmacist whether to take it after meals.
You have to rest at home today.

extendedDialogue.setting: A clinic visit moves from symptoms to medicine instructions and follow-up advice.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Where does it hurt? What brings you in?
lines.grammarNote: 아파서 connects the symptom to the clinic visit.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.ko: 아침부터 열이 나고 목이 아파요. 기침도 나요.
lines.romanization: achimbuteo yeori nago mogi apayo. gichimdo nayo.
lines.en: Since this morning I have had a fever and a sore throat. I also have a cough.
lines.grammarNote: 열이 나다, 목이 아프다, and 기침이 나다 are symptom phrases.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.ko: 감기 때문에 그런 것 같아요. 약은 식후에 하루 세 번 드셔야 해요.
lines.romanization: gamgi ttaemune geureon geot gatayo. yageun sikhue haru se beon deusyeoya haeyo.
lines.en: It seems to be because of a cold. You have to take the medicine three times a day after meals.
lines.grammarNote: 때문에 names the cause; 드셔야 해요 gives an instruction.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.ko: 기침 때문에 잠을 못 자면 다시 와야 하나요?
lines.romanization: gichim ttaemune jameul mot jamyeon dasi waya hanayo?
lines.en: If I cannot sleep because of the cough, should I come back?
lines.grammarNote: 기침 때문에 explains the blocked action.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.ko: 네. 열이 계속 나니까 물을 많이 마시고 쉬세요.
lines.romanization: ne. yeori gyesok nanikka mureul mani masigo swiseyo.
lines.en: Yes. Since the fever is continuing, drink a lot of water and rest.
lines.grammarNote: 니까 gives the reason for advice.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.ko: 네. 처방전을 받고 약국에 가서 약을 기다릴게요.
lines.romanization: ne. cheobangjeoneul batgo yakguge gaseo yageul gidarilgeyo.
lines.en: Okay. I will take the prescription, go to the pharmacy, and wait for the medicine.
lines.grammarNote: The patient repeats the practical next steps after hearing the instructions.

readingText.title: 약은 식후에 하루 세 번 드세요
readingText.body: 민수는 아침부터 열이 나고 목이 아파서 동네 병원에 갔어요. 의사 선생님은 감기 때문에 그런 것 같다고 말했어요. 기침이 심해지는 바람에 어젯밤에는 잠도 거의 못 잤어요. 민수는 처방전을 받아서 약국에 갔고, 약사에게 복약 방법을 들었어요. 약은 식후에 하루 세 번 먹어야 하고, 열이 계속 나니까 물을 많이 마시고 쉬어야 해요. 증상이 나아지지 않으면 다시 병원에 와야 해요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minsu had a fever and sore throat from the morning, so he went to a neighborhood clinic. The doctor said it seemed to be because of a cold. Because his cough got worse, he barely slept the night before. Minsu got a prescription and went to the pharmacy, where he heard the medicine instructions from the pharmacist. He has to take the medicine three times a day after meals, and since the fever is continuing, he has to drink a lot of water and rest. If the symptoms do not improve, he has to go back to the clinic.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민수는 왜 병원에 갔어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 열이 나고 목이 아파서 병원에 갔어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 기침이 심해지는 바람에 무엇을 못 했어요?
약은 언제, 얼마나 먹어야 해요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 식후에 하루 세 번 먹어야 해요.

culturalNote.title: Clinic and pharmacy flow
culturalNote.body: In Korea, many neighborhood clinics are paired with nearby pharmacies. The clinic gives a 처방전, and the pharmacy prepares medicine by dose. That is why phrases like 하루 세 번, 식후, 식전, 자기 전, and 며칠분 are practical, not optional.
culturalNote.tip: At the clinic, lead with symptoms and time: 아침부터, 어제부터, 열이 나요, 목이 아파요. At the pharmacy, confirm timing and frequency: 식후에요? 하루 몇 번이에요?

inlineExercises.explanation: 열이 나다 and 목이 아프다 are natural symptom frames.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence names a symptom as the cause?
inlineExercises.explanation: N 때문에 attaches directly to the noun.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which instruction means 'You have to take the medicine after meals'?
inlineExercises.explanation: 식후에 gives timing; 드셔야 해요 gives a necessary instruction.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 는 바람에 for an unwanted disruption?
options: 기침이 심해지는 바람에 잠을 못 잤어요.
기침이 심해지는 덕분에 잠을 못 잤어요.
기침이 심해지는 중에 잠을 못 자야 해요.
inlineExercises.correct: 기침이 심해지는 바람에 잠을 못 잤어요.
inlineExercises.explanation: 는 바람에 fits an unwanted cause that disrupted sleep.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence reports a current pharmacy action?
inlineExercises.explanation: V-는 중이에요 reports an action in progress.

bullets: Symptom frames: 목이 아파요, 배가 아파요, 열이 나요, 기침이 나요.
Clinic flow: 병원에서 증상을 말하고 처방전을 받아요.
Pharmacy flow: 약국에서 약을 받고 식후/하루 세 번을 확인해요.
Cause choices: 아파서 is neutral, 때문에 names the problem, 니까 leads to advice, 는 바람에 implies disruption.
Instruction frame: 약은 식후에 드셔야 해요.
